Requirement: The system shall acquire thermal frames of the solar panel and process them to identify hotspots on the panel.
The system shall measure each photovoltaic panel voltage output (0–25 VDC range) with at least 9 bits of precision.
The system shall measure each photovoltaic panel current output (0–5 A range) with at least 9 bits of precision.
The system shall estimate each panel’s real-time power efficiency by comparing the measured instantaneous power against the panel’s rated power.
The system shall transmit measurement data (temperature, voltage, current, power, status) to the cloud via a Wi-Fi connection.
The system shall control the nozzle tilt servo via PWM signal, sweeping the angle from ~−60° to 0° over a duration of 3–5 seconds when a cleaning cycle is triggered.
The water pump shall be driven via a MOSFET module or relay module and activated for a defined duration (3–5 seconds) upon hotspot confirmation.
The system shall control the stepper motor to position the sensing/cleaning module at every panel strip in a linear motion.
The system shall regulate and distribute power from a 12V 5A DC supply to the microcontroller, sensors, servos, and pump circuits.
The instant voltage and current snapshots shall be taken every 15-30 minutes or before every cycle of hotspot detection and shall run for at least 60 seconds with at least 2 measurements per second.
The system shall use the INA219 module to capture voltage and current snapshots and connect to the main controller via I2C.
The system shall save non-volatile data in a MicroSD card though a reader module connected to the controller via SPI.

The electronic components (ESP32, power converters, drivers and switching modules) shall be housed in 3D-printed enclosures made of PETG, providing a degree of protection of at least IP54 according to IEC 60529.
The system shall use the LM2596 module to stepdown the 12V bus to 5V.
The system shall control the camera tilt servo via PWM signal, sweeping the angle from ~−60° to 0° to ensure a proper FOV for the thermal frame capturing.
The system shall include Normally Closed (NC) microswitches to serve as physical hardware limit failsafes.
The system shall use an LED to represent its current state (idle, sensing, cleaning, no wi-fi connection, low water on reservoir).
The water reservoir level shall be measured with the JSN-SR04T ultrassonic sensor.
The system shall use the MLX90640 thermal camera to capture thermal frames and send data to the microcontroller via I2C.
Bench tests shall be done with a dimmer controlled by another ESP32 and a Halogen/LED lamp with at least 100W.
